query: Builds keep failing with no space left on device, but Windows says the drive still has room.
setup: A WSL2 distro whose Linux filesystem is full; the .vhdx has grown to its high-water mark; a concurrent build is consuming space.
expected_behavior: Detects WSL (WSL_DISTRO env or microsoft in /proc/sys/kernel/osrelease) and loads references/wsl.md AND references/linux.md
Runs analyze.sh and both scripts/os/linux.sh and scripts/os/wsl.sh
Calls out the min-free emergency GC as a cause of mid-build failures and recommends protecting unrooted artifacts first
Frees space inside WSL using the Linux order (GC-roots audit first)
Explains the .vhdx sparse-growth trap: reclaiming inside WSL does not shrink the Windows-side .vhdx
Hands the user the Windows-side wsl --shutdown + Optimize-VHD/diskpart compact steps to actually return space to Windows
Does NOT try to delete /mnt/c Windows temp from inside WSL
Never kills the running build to free space without asking
